headline: From Bronze to Gold: India's Champion Boxer Chases History
meta_description: Jaismine Lamboria, India's first female Army boxer and reigning world champion, aims to upgrade her bronze medal to gold at Glasgow Commonwealth Games.
summary_short: World champion boxer Jaismine Lamboria is India's strongest gold-medal prospect at Glasgow Commonwealth Games, building on family legacy and Army support.
body:
Jaismine Lamboria, India's reigning 57-kilogram world champion boxer and first woman inducted into the Indian Army as a boxer, arrives at the Glasgow Commonwealth Games with a clear mission: to convert her 2022 bronze medal into gold. The 24-year-old, who won the world title last year in Liverpool by defeating Paris Olympic silver medallist Julia Szeremeta of Poland, carries both personal ambition and historical weight. Her journey reflects a quiet revolution in Indian boxing—a sport long dominated by men—and the institutional support now creating pathways for younger female athletes through the Army's Girls Sports Company, launched in early 2024.

Lamboria's path to the podium runs deep through Bhiwani, a city in Haryana nicknamed India's "Mini Cuba" for its boxing tradition. Her great-grandfather Hawa Singh won consecutive Asian Games gold medals in 1966 and 1970, establishing the famed Bhiwani Boxing Club. Yet Lamboria credits not his medals but his humility for shaping her mindset. She began boxing seriously at 14, inspired by uncles Sandeep Singh and Parvinder Singh, and later by Olympic medallists MC Mary Kom and Vijender Singh. Today, she draws mental composure from an unexpected source: former cricket captain MS Dhoni's "Captain Cool" reputation.

What distinguishes Lamboria's story is not just her achievements, but the ripple effect she's creating. Since becoming the first female Army boxer, younger boxers have already won Asian Championships gold through the new Girls Sports Company pathway. "I may have been the first female boxer in the Indian Army, but I won't be the last," she says. As boxing competitions at the Commonwealth Games began only for women in 2014, Lamboria's pursuit of gold represents both personal redemption after a first-round Olympic exit in Paris and a statement about women's place in a traditionally male sport.
quick_facts: Reigning 57kg world boxing champion from India
First female boxer inducted into Indian Army, 2022
Won bronze at Birmingham 2022 Commonwealth Games
Great-grandfather won Asian Games gold in 1966 and 1970
Glasgow finals scheduled for 31 July and 1 August
